usageNotes: Use this endpoint to synchronously update VM configuration settings such as CPU, memory, network, boot order, cloud-init parameters, or description — any change that does not require hotplug or storage allocation. For operations involving hotplug (attaching devices to a running VM) or allocating new disk volumes, use POST /nodes/{node}/qemu/{vmid}/config instead, which queues the change asynchronously and returns a UPID. The caller must hold at least one matching VM.Config.* privilege on /vms/{vmid} for the specific parameter category being changed.

examples.summary: Resize CPU and memory, update description, and enable QEMU guest agent on VM 200

tips: Pass the 'digest' param (from GET /config) to prevent overwriting concurrent changes — the API will reject the request if the config has changed since you read it.
To remove a config key (e.g., a network device or unused tag), use the 'delete' param with a comma-separated list of key names rather than omitting them.
Deleting a disk key without 'force: true' moves the volume to unused[n] rather than destroying it; set force=true only when you intend permanent removal.
Cloud-init params (ciuser, cipassword, ipconfig[n], etc.) take effect on the next VM start — they do not reconfigure a running instance.
Changes to CPU or memory on a running VM are not applied until the VM is next stopped and started unless those resources are hotplugged via the POST variant.
